title: Badlands
body: The Badlands are a cracked desert of dry earth and winding canyons in the southeast of Khaz Modan, where coyotes, buzzards and restless rock elementals roam the flats. Treasure draws visitors all the same. In the north lie the ruins of Uldaman, a vault of the titans, where the diggers of Ironforge have been slaughtered by Stonevault troggs woken from long slumber and by the Shadowforge clan of Dark Irons. Dustbelcher ogres camp across the land, the black dragonflight nests in Lethlor Ravine, and at Kargath the Horde keeps its only outpost in Khaz Modan.

title: Kargath
body: Kargath, named for the Shattered Hand chieftain Kargath Bladefist, is the only Horde outpost in all of Khaz Modan, and so close to Alliance-held Loch Modan that it is often cut off from Stonard. It is the headquarters of the Kargath Expeditionary Force, sent by the Warchief under Warlord Goretooth to strike at the renegade Blackrock orcs and their Dark Iron allies in Blackrock Mountain, and its posted orders call for the death of Dark Iron dwarves on sight.

parts.body: Since the blood elves joined the Horde, an advisor from Quel'Thalas has come too, expecting a headquarters and finding what he calls a hovel of uncouth, sniggering savages.

title: Hammertoe's Digsite
body: In the north of the Badlands, not far from Uldaman, lies the excavation of Hammertoe Grez, who worked with the Explorers' League seeking the origins of his people among the titan ruins. The Shadowforge clan fell on the site without warning and killed nearly everyone. Their tunnelers still pick through the abandoned camp, and the few survivors gathered just to the south, where Prospector Ryedol mourns his boss and plots to recover what was lost.

parts.body: A crumpled map in the dirt carries Hammertoe's own chalked message: the Shadowforge did not kill him with the rest, but dragged him away to Uldaman.
sources: quest 719 description (Shadowforge attack killed nearly everyone, site just north of Ryedol)

parts.body: Hammertoe was found in the ruins, beaten and coughing, and sent his amulet, his life's work, back to Ryedol. He did not live to see it arrive.

title: Angor Fortress
body: Angor Fortress is the Dark Iron stronghold of the northern Badlands, the base from which the Shadowforge clan organizes its digging in Uldaman. Shadowforge warriors and stone golems crowd its halls, and among them dwells Ambassador Infernus, a creature of living fire sent by Ragnaros himself to watch over the hunt for titan artifacts that might be turned against Ironforge. King Magni's council has ordered him destroyed.

title: Dustbelch Grotto
body: Dustbelch Grotto, a cave in the far southwest, is the main home of the Dustbelcher ogres, whose camps are scattered across the Badlands. Ogre lords hold court here among mages, maulers and shamans, and the grotto's ogres go well supplied with scrap metal. The Dustbelcher once fought for the Horde, but they are part of it no longer, and some of their bands now sell their strength to whoever pays.

title: Agmond's End
body: In the south of the Badlands, past Angor Fortress, lies the smallest of the Ironforge excavations, where Prospector Agmond, who had charge of the dwarven digs in these lands, was last known to be working. Word from him stopped coming weeks ago. Stonevault troggs now hold the site, and close by the mad hermit Theldurin the Lost has made his camp.

parts.body: Agmond never left the desert. His skeleton lay here, picked clean, at the end of a trail of bloody smears where he had crawled from the west, and beside his hand a single name was scratched into the sandstone: Murdaloc.

title: Lethlor Ravine
body: In the far east of the Badlands a deep ravine cuts through the mountains, and it belongs to the black dragonflight: scalding whelps swarm its floor and scorched drakes keep watch. The ravine holds an older secret, the Seal of the Earth, a prison held shut by runestones set in three pillars of amethyst, opal and diamond, which only the Sign of the Earth can draw out.

parts.body: The prisoners are the twin drakes Blacklash and Hematus, lieutenants of Deathwing and allies of the Horde in the Second War, bound by the Dark Irons of Angor Fortress. Their key was stolen by the ogre mercenaries hired to fetch it.
sources: quest 717 and 793 descriptions (Seal, runestones, Pillars of Amethyst, Opal and Diamond)

parts.body: Rather than trust the Seal any longer, Horde and Alliance alike chose to break it, and Blacklash and Hematus rose from their prison only to die at the hands of those who freed them.

title: Lotwil Veriatus
body: Lotwil Veriatus is a gnome of Kharanos and a scholar of renown in the elemental sciences, camped in the Dustbowl east of Kargath, where there are raw materials and open space for spells that might go wrong. There he perfects shackles of elemental binding, which he believes will let mages command elementals mightier than any summoned before. He is brilliant, absent-minded and forever muttering, and his assistant Lucien prefers to watch from behind cover.

parts.body: Lotwil has a darker past than his mutterings suggest. When shards etched with the initials G.L.A. were brought to him from the golems of the Burning Steppes, the gnome went white: he knew those markings.

title: Theldurin the Lost
body: Theldurin the Lost was once a member of the Twilight's Hammer, until he lost his mind and turned against the cult's teachings, stealing a scroll his former brethren prize before he fled. Now he lives in a lonely camp in the southern Badlands, gibbering to himself and confessing that being crazy is sometimes his only solace. He fears an approaching doom whose bringers he dares not name, and hunts for any lore that might foil them.

parts.body: The stolen scroll is the Scroll of Myzrael, whose magic can pull Myzrael to the surface world. If she is already free, he reasons, it will be needed to trap her again, and enraged elementals have torn it to pieces.
sources: quest 687 description (once a member, lost his mind, scorned teachings, stole the scroll, hides in Badlands gibbering and mad)

parts.body: With a tablet from Uldaman and a book his old brethren study, Theldurin seeks a way to foil the doom he will not name, and fears the worst: if they are ever freed and rise to the surface, he says, the world is worm food.
